newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka stocks take breather in long slump, end firm.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka stocks take breather in long slump, end firm.

text.p: Dhaka stocks took a break from a three-week old slump and closed nearly one percent higher as selling pressure from retail investors eased, brokers said.
The Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) benchmark index rose 19.64 points or 0.87 percent to 2,261.47 on turnover of 26.9 million taka. Of 73 traded issues, 51 gained, 21 lost and one unchanged.

Broker Moshtaque Ahmed said market would soon regain confidence following a "fruitful" meeting between Finance Minister SAMS Kibria and the stock exchange council Sunday on the market's weakness over the last month.
"Many misunderstandings are now over (between the stock exchange and the government)," he said.

The market has tumbled recently after a thundering rally from around 800-900 last June to as much as 3,700 this autumn. The market watchdog agency, fearing a bubble, imposed a limit on price movements of five percent, bringing the euphoria to an end. A few market watchers also believe the recent slide is a necessary correction.
IDLC rose 178 taka to 4,775 and Monno Fabrics gained 11 to 239.
